transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Will. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Will. Our S-Net TV multi-room mini box in our master bedroom has completely stopped working. It says Server Connection Error CS1011, and our main TV 360 box downstairs is working fine. The bedroom box connects through Powerline adapters in the wall sockets, and it was working perfectly until yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating it is when your bedroom TV mini box loses connection and prevents you from watching your shows, Emily. Let me look into your multi-room account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Will, my elderly mother is staying with us in the bedroom and she relies on the TV for company.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we check your multi-room profile, Emily, could you verify your installation postcode and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 16 Queens Drive, Nottingham, NG2 1GB, and the PIN is 6249.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Emily. I have your TV 360 multi-room profile open in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what is happening: your main S-Net TV 360 box downstairs is operating normally, but your upstairs bedroom mini box has lost connection to the main box with error CS1011, communicating over Powerline network adapters. Is that correct, Emily?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. Downstairs has full live TV and recordings, but upstairs is completely offline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Powerline network adapters transmit data over household copper mains wiring, which is subject to severe electrical noise whenever household appliances like refrigerators, microwave ovens, or washing machines cycle on and off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nothing has changed with our appliances, Will. The adapters worked without a hitch for nine months.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Electrical wiring degrades over time, and S-Net does not manufacture, supply, or warranty third-party Powerline hardware. We cannot support third-party electrical wiring devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I bought these specific Powerline adapters directly from the S-Net online accessories store when we ordered the multi-room package! Your installer even plugged them in for us!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand that you purchased them from our accessory store, Emily, but Powerline technology is fundamentally dependent on your home's consumer unit fuse box. You really need to contact the adapter manufacturer TP-Link or have an electrician inspect your circuit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will, I am not calling an electrician to look at two plug sockets when the TV box is showing an S-Net error code CS1011! Can't you at least check if the mini box is communicating with the main box on your diagnostics?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me run a remote multi-room handshake audit on your Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the remote handshake audit show?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The audit indicates that the main TV 360 box is online at IP 192.168.1.15, but the mini box at IP 192.168.1.28 is failing the ARP discovery ping.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the mini box is not getting through the network to the main box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the local network path is broken between the two endpoints.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we reset the mini box network settings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can unplug the bedroom mini box from the power socket for thirty seconds and plug it back in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugging the mini box now... waiting thirty seconds... plugging the power cable back in... the blue light is flashing on the front of the box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait until the blue light turns solid white on the front panel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's flashing for about a minute... and now error CS1011 popped right back up on the TV screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now look at the Powerline adapter plugged into the wall next to the bedroom TV box. What lights are showing on it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The power light is green, the Ethernet light is green, but the middle light with the little house icon is completely unlit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The house icon represents the encrypted Powerline link between the two plug adapters. When it is unlit, the two adapters have lost their paired synchronization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the adapters just need to be re-paired together?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. On the side of the bedroom Powerline adapter, press and hold the Pair button for two seconds until the power light blinks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressing the Pair button for two seconds... okay, the power LED is blinking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now you must go downstairs to the Powerline adapter plugged in next to your main Hub router and press its Pair button for two seconds within two minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running downstairs to the hallway... pressing the Pair button on the router adapter... holding for two seconds... its power light is blinking too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait about thirty seconds for the 128-bit AES encryption keys to exchange across the electrical wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looking at the hallway adapter... the house icon light just turned solid green!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now check the bedroom adapter upstairs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Walking back upstairs to the bedroom... the house icon on the bedroom adapter is solid green now too!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Both adapters have successfully re-established their physical powerline link.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the TV screen just refreshed! It says Connecting to main box... and live BBC One loaded! The picture and sound are playing perfectly!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you able to open the Recordings menu and verify that your shared cloud recordings from downstairs are accessible?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Saved Recordings... yes, all our recorded series and movies are listed with full playback!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The CS1011 handshake error is fully cleared now that the Powerline connection has synchronized.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am so relieved we didn't need to call an electrician after all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Power surges or minor voltage fluctuations can occasionally disrupt the encryption handshake between adapters.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that I know how to press the pair buttons, I can easily fix it if it ever happens again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are there any tips to prevent the Powerline adapters from losing sync in the future?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Always ensure Powerline adapters are plugged directly into permanent wall sockets rather than multi-way extension leads or surge protectors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both of ours are plugged directly into dedicated wall faceplates with no extension leads.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Plugging into wall sockets minimizes RF attenuation and harmonic distortion across the ring main.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And if we ever want to add a third TV box in the study, can we add a third Powerline adapter to the same network?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, up to eight compatible Powerline adapters can participate in the same encrypted home network cluster by using the same pairing button sequence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will make expanding our TV setup very straightforward when we renovate the study.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should I do if the house icon light goes red instead of green in the future?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A red link light indicates low bandwidth below thirty megabits, usually caused by plugging into an extension socket next to a high-draw appliance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, so keeping it in a direct socket ensures a solid green link.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your multi-room TV service that I can check for you today, Emily?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Will, once we re-paired the plugs everything came back to life. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Emily. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Will, goodbye.
